subject.title: MEDIA: tokens inside markdown code fences are silently ignored

question: Should fenced final-reply `MEDIA:` lines remain non-delivered with a warning, be extracted when valid and standalone, or be documented as invalid with no runtime diagnostic?
rationale: Current source intentionally preserves fenced examples as text, but the reported problem is silent attachment loss; extraction changes transcript semantics, while warn-only makes the failure diagnosable without changing delivery.

options.title: Land warn-only diagnostics
options.body: Keep fenced `MEDIA:` lines as visible text but emit one clear warning at the real outbound delivery boundary when delivery was likely intended.

options.title: Extract fenced standalone tokens
options.body: Treat valid standalone fenced `MEDIA:` lines as attachments, accepting the risk that example snippets may become deliveries.

options.title: Document as invalid only
options.body: Leave runtime behavior unchanged and rely on docs and prompt guidance to prevent invalid fenced legacy directives.

recommendation.title: Land warn-only diagnostics
recommendation.body: Keep fenced `MEDIA:` lines as visible text but emit one clear warning at the real outbound delivery boundary when delivery was likely intended.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the live reviewer on the candidate PR and have recent parser/reply-boundary history.
